confirmed.what_breaks: A failed line save on a long order shows no error in view: the banner lands under the h1 while focus jumps to Save far below, so the form reads as if Save did nothing.
confirmed.evidence: order-view.js:277 commit fails, :279 showBanner(code); main.js:64 querySelector('[data-banner-region]') returns the one region the view placed at :335 directly under the h1, and lineForm (:136-154) builds no region of its own. :280 ui.save.focus() then scrolls the Save button into view. styles.css:54 sets --row-height 2.75rem, so 20 lines put 55rem (880px) between the banner and Save, beyond a usual viewport. UI-SPEC lines 130 and 438: with a form open the banner goes at the top of that form's panel; line 425 keeps the page region only for Remove. R-21 is a MUST (the app shows an error) and storage full plus a long order is an input a user can produce (MANUAL-CHECKS.md:117 describes filling storage). The banner keeps role=alert, so only sighted users miss it.

confirmed.what_breaks: No test pins the write lock after a load whose getItem throws: a planted defect that leaves canWrite true survives, so save() would write over a store that could not be read.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: storage.js:31 'canWrite = false' became 'canWrite = true' and all 421 tests passed. With the mutant, a backing whose getItem throws returns unavailable at :36 with canWrite still true, so save() at :48 skips the blocked answer and calls setItem; the original answers { ok: false, reason: 'blocked' }. ADR-004 line 37: save answers blocked until the last load or erase succeeded, and a test can prove it. tests/storage.test.js:24 covers save before any load and nothing covers save after a throwing getItem; tests/storage.spec.mjs:335-507 cover corrupt, newer and a throwing localStorage access, none of which this mutant changes. The UI never reaches the path today (main.js:191 renders the blocked screen), so no user loses data now.

confirmed.what_breaks: The quantity rule is neither the one ADR-007 decided nor pinned by a test: a planted defect widening the pattern survives, and a zero-padded value such as 000005 is refused although it is 5.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: validation.js:7 /^\d{1,5}$/ became /^\d{1,6}$/ and all 421 tests passed. Input '000005': the original parseQuantity (:98) returns null and the form shows line.quantity.invalid; the mutant returns 5 and accepts the line, while '00005' passes both. ADR-007 line 15: quantity is trimmed text matching ^\d+$, then the range 1 to MAX_QUANTITY, so the mutant is closer to the decision than the code (COR-11, SEC-11, CON-11 report the same deviation). tests/validation.test.js:115-127 try '0', '10000', '2.0', '1e3', '-1', '', '+1', 'two' and never a six-digit zero-padded value; tests/validation.spec.mjs:210-216 neither. Fix: the ADR-007 pattern plus tests that '000005' is stored as 5 and '100000' is refused by the range.

confirmed.what_breaks: R-15 is tested only on its refusal side: a planted defect moving the safe-total boundary by one survives, and a total of exactly Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER would be refused.
confirmed.evidence: mutate.mjs: lines.js:20 reduce start value 0 became 1 and all 421 tests passed. Input: an order with one line of quantity 1 and unitPriceCents 9007199254740990 (a safe integer, accepted by shape.js:12), then addLine of quantity '1' at unit price '0.01': the original sums to 9007199254740991, Number.isSafeInteger true, ok; the mutant sums to 9007199254740992, not safe, and answers line.total.too-large. tests/lines.test.js:39-44 and tests/lines.spec.mjs:229 assert only the refusal above the limit, never the largest accepted total. Through the forms the same total takes about 9008 largest lines, so no user meets it; the boundary test is still owed by AGENTS.md rule 2.

confirmed.what_breaks: Deleting an order while a dirty line form is open asks 'Discard your changes?' after the delete; Keep editing leaves the deleted order on screen, then Cancel throws APP-01 and Save line drops the typed text.
confirmed.evidence: deleteButton (order-view.js:178, listener :323) is never disabled while ui.open is true; only addButton (:206) and the row buttons (:74-75) are. Path: Add line, type 'x', Delete order, confirm. confirmDelete :315 commits, :320 location.replace('#/orders') leaves state.form set. main.js:182-184: the hash differs, form.isDirty() is true ('x' !== ''), askToDiscard opens. Keep editing: main.js:175 sets location.hash back to the deleted order's hash, which equals renderedHash, so :182 returns without a render and the stale screen stays. Cancel: cancelForm, closeForm, drawLines :205 currentOrder() is undefined and :207 now.lines throws TypeError, main.js:197 shows APP-01. Save line: addLine finds no order, NOT_FOUND, :274 renderNotFound, the typed text is gone. Advisory: the user asked for the delete and only text typed for the deleted order is lost.

confirmed.what_breaks: Keep editing throws APP-01 when focus was last on Save line or Cancel in the line form, which is exactly where a failed save puts it; Reload then loses the typed line.

confirmed.what_breaks: A newly saved customer is hidden by a search text kept from before: the user lands on 'No customers match this search.' right after saving.
confirmed.evidence: customer-list.js:97 input.value = state.searchCustomers and :114 showResults filters with it; customer-form.js:56 targets() sends a saved new customer to '#/customers' and nothing resets state.searchCustomers on the way. Input: search 'zzz', New customer, save 'Ana': searchCustomers(data, 'zzz') returns [] and the list shows the no-match state with 'zzz' in the box. R-01 (MUST): 'then the customer appears in the list'. ADR-005 line 46 (accepted): search texts 'survive moving between screens'. Both hold at once only if a save clears or bypasses the search, which neither document says; the human answers. Advisory: the customer is saved and the box shows why it is hidden.

confirmed.what_breaks: A document that passes the shape check can still make every order screen throw, so a hand-edited data set gives APP-01 with Reload instead of the R-20 blocked screen, and the records cannot be opened or deleted except through Erase all data.
confirmed.evidence: shape.js:17 checks date only with isText and :12 checks quantity and unitPriceCents only with isCount. Input 1 (SEC-1): an order with date 'not-a-date' loads ok; format.js:14 new Date('not-a-dateT00:00:00Z') is Invalid Date and Intl.DateTimeFormat.format throws RangeError from order-list.js:51, customer-detail.js:69 and order-view.js:30. Input 2 (SEC-2): quantity 9007199254740991 and unitPriceCents 2 pass isCount; lineTotalCents gives about 1.8e16 and money.js:25 throws from orders.js:26 on #/orders and from order-view.js:91, so the order and its customer (R-04) stay locked; unitPriceCents -50 also passes and priceInputText gives '-1.-50'. main.js:197 shows APP-01 with Reload only. ADR-004 line 33 names the purpose of the check (no lock-out) and the sketch types date as YYYY-MM-DD, so a date format check and a safe-total check are the invariants the screens rely on, not form rules. Hand-edited data only.

confirmed.what_breaks: The order-number invariants are not enforced on stored data: a negative or maximal nextOrderNumber makes the app write a document it refuses on the next load, and two orders can share a sequence number.
confirmed.evidence: shape.js:53 isCount accepts any safe integer. Input 1: nextOrderNumber -5 with no orders: orders.js:7 gives 'ORD-' + String(-5).padStart(4, '0') = 'ORD-00-5', save succeeds, and on the next load ORDER_NUMBER /^ORD-(\d+)$/ fails at shape.js:18, so the document the app itself wrote is corrupt. Input 2: nextOrderNumber 9007199254740991: createOrder stores 9007199254740992, isCount is false, corrupt. SEC-4 (merged): 'ORD-1' and 'ORD-0001' are distinct strings for allUnique at :42 while orderNumberValue gives 1 for both and both sit below nextOrderNumber 2, so the document passes and two orders show the same sequence. ADR-004 line 15: the counter starts at 1. Hand-edited data only.

confirmed.what_breaks: Unknown keys in a stored document are kept, written back on every save and, on a customer, copied into the R-29 export, so personal data outside the sketch survives every delete.
confirmed.evidence: hasValidShape checks named fields only; storage.js:22 keeps every other key in data; commands spread ...data (customers.js:20, orders.js:44) and save :50 writes it back. Input: nationalId on a customer: export.js:11 structuredClone copies it into the export, while updateCustomer :29 rebuilds the record from id plus checked fields and drops it, so two paths disagree. ADR-004 line 12: the fields of the sketch 'and nothing added'; line 57: shape.js refuses rather than repairs. Hand-edited data only.

confirmed.what_breaks: Stored ids are accepted as any string and put raw into the hash, so some hand-edited records cannot be opened or open another screen, and cannot be deleted through their own screen.
confirmed.evidence: shape.js:8 isText accepts '' and any text for id; router.js:51-57 interpolate r.id unencoded. Input id '': href '#/customers/', parseRoute :41 refuses the empty part, not-found. Input id 'new': '#/customers/new' opens the new-customer form (router.js:19). Input id 'a b': location.hash holds a%20b, parseRoute does not decode, the find at customer-detail.js:133 fails, not-found. Line id '': order-view.js:229 treats '' as no line and Edit opens Add. The value stays inside the fragment, so no script URL results. The app's own ids are UUIDs; hand-edited data only.

confirmed.what_breaks: A name or description made only of invisible characters passes the required-field check, so a customer or a line can be saved with no visible text.
confirmed.evidence: validation.js:33 trim() removes only ECMAScript WhiteSpace and LineTerminator (category Zs plus TAB, VT, FF, FEFF); U+200B is category Cf and stays. Input name '\u200B': length 1, lengthError at :62 passes, createCustomer stores it; customer-list.js:32 renders a row link with no visible text. Same path for description at :105-109. R-01's letter (1 to 100 characters after trimming) is met, so whether invisible-only text counts as empty is the human's call.

confirmed.what_breaks: On a plain http origin other than localhost (a LAN address), crypto.randomUUID is undefined, so every create throws TypeError and shows APP-01; no customer or order can be added.
confirmed.evidence: main.js:49 deps.newId calls crypto.randomUUID() with no check; the Web Crypto IDL declares randomUUID [SecureContext], so on http://192.168.x.x:8000 the property is undefined, customers.js:19 throws TypeError and main.js:197 shows APP-01. ADR-008 line 11 names only http://localhost:8000/ and https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/, both secure contexts, and its T-02 answer says real data runs 'from localhost or from an origin of their own'. The human says whether a LAN http origin is such an origin; if yes, newId needs crypto.getRandomValues, which has no secure-context limit. No browser ran here; the IDL is the evidence.

confirmed.what_breaks: The sticky table header never sticks while the page scrolls, because every table panel is an overflow: hidden scroll container.

confirmed.what_breaks: Above 2^46 cents a shown total can be one cent off although addLine accepts it as safe; a theoretical limit at about 70 trillion euros.
confirmed.evidence: format.js:8 divides cents by 100 in double precision. For cents = 9007199254740987 (safe, accepted by lines.js:21) the exact quotient 90071992547409.87 lies in [2^46, 2^47), where doubles are 1/64 apart: the nearest double is 90071992547409.875 and Intl.NumberFormat rounds that half to '...409.88', one cent above the stored total. Below 2^46 (about 7.04e15 cents) the spacing is under 0.01 and the rounding is exact. Reaching it takes about 7042 largest lines. Fix without a decision: format from integer division and remainder (as priceInputText does) or pass a decimal string to Intl.NumberFormat.format. Shown by arithmetic; not executed here.

confirmed.what_breaks: No test covers years 0000 to 0099, so removing the setUTCFullYear line passes every test while '0099-01-01' would be refused.
confirmed.evidence: dates.js:9 setUTCFullYear(year) exists because Date.UTC maps 0 to 99 onto 1900 to 1999. tests/dates.test.js:5-11 and tests/dates.spec.mjs:23 (accepts 2026-02-28, 2024-02-29, 2000-02-29, 2026-12-31, 2026-01-01) and its refusal list use no year below 1000; grep for '00dd-' under tests/ finds nothing. watchList.what_breaks: The blob URL is revoked in the same task as link.click(); a browser that starts the download later could drop it with no error shown.
watchList.evidence: customer-detail.js:113-115 run link.click(), link.remove(), URL.revokeObjectURL(url) with nothing in between.
watchList.why_unproven: Chromium captures the blob at click time; Firefox and Safari behaviour cannot be shown without a browser. Same cause as SEC-13.
watchList.how_to_settle: Run the R-29 line of MANUAL-CHECKS.md (line 78) in current Firefox and Safari and check the file arrives with its full content.

watchList.what_breaks: Same path as COR-14: an export that silently does not arrive.
watchList.evidence: downloadExport revokes the URL right after click() with no wait.
watchList.why_unproven: Not shown to fail in any current browser; no browser ran here.
watchList.how_to_settle: The R-29 manual check in Chromium, Firefox and Safari.

watchList.what_breaks: save() trusts its caller: a malformed value or a stray version key would overwrite good data or change the version.
watchList.evidence: storage.js:50 spreads data after version, so save({ version: 2, ... }) writes version 2 and save({}) writes a document the next load calls corrupt. Every caller passes result.data from a domain command and parseDocument :22 strips version, so no path reaches it today.
watchList.why_unproven: No reachable caller; a hardening question, not an observed defect.
watchList.how_to_settle: A storage test calling save after a good load with a value lacking customers and one with a version key pins the contract; the human says whether save must re-check the shape (ADR-004 lists no such check).

watchList.what_breaks: A non-SyntaxError from JSON.parse would escape load() before the error listeners exist, leaving a blank page; writing stays locked.
watchList.evidence: storage.js:15 rethrows anything but SyntaxError; createStorage.load :42 has no try around parseDocument; main.js:189 calls load() before the listeners at :197-198.
watchList.why_unproven: Real localStorage returns a string or null, so only an engine error (out of memory on a huge text) could trigger it; none was produced.
watchList.how_to_settle: A storage test whose backing returns a value that makes JSON.parse throw a non-SyntaxError, asserting load() returns a result instead of throwing; or a manual check with a stored text near the quota in each target browser.

watchList.what_breaks: The export's purpose and retention texts carry project ids (R-04, R-08, A-10) and backticked field names the person receiving the file cannot look up.
watchList.evidence: export.js:3-5 hold the texts; ADR-007 line 49 fixes them as frozen texts from A-13 and A-14; R-29 asks that the user can answer an access request with the file. LD-06 asks for purpose and retention, which the file does state.
watchList.why_unproven: Whether the internal references make the statement unfit for the person is a reading between two documents the human approved; not a legal judgement I make.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human answers under docs/decisions whether the frozen texts stay or get a plain-language version; a change needs a new accepted ADR text.

watchList.what_breaks: A-13 names notes and line description as fields that should hold no details about other people, but only the notes field carries the warning helper.
watchList.evidence: order-form.js:8 NOTES_HELPER carries the warning; order-view.js:147 gives Description no helper; UI-SPEC line 432 (approved) sets the Description helper to none, so the build matches the spec. REQUIREMENTS.md:168 lists OrderLine description as personal data when it names a person.
watchList.why_unproven: LD-03 is about storing only needed data by default; a missing hint is not a stored field, and the approved spec chose none. Whether the spec row stands is the human's call.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human says whether UI-SPEC line 432 stands or Description gets the same helper as Notes.

watchList.what_breaks: An order's customerId, listed as personal data, is corrected only by deleting the order and rebuilding it, which retypes every line and uses up a number.
watchList.evidence: A-06 (REQUIREMENTS.md:143, confirmed by the human) makes delete and re-create the path; validation.js:92 and order-form.js:73 implement it. LD-04 asks that correction is possible and reaches every place it is shown; it is possible at that cost.
watchList.why_unproven: Whether the cost fails 'without undue delay' is a legal reading of a decision the human already took; I give no legal advice.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human confirms A-06 under LD-04 in docs/decisions, or asks for an order move command in a new slice.

watchList.what_breaks: The accepted answer to threat T-02 rests on a runbook that does not exist, and the app's own note says nothing about the shared github.io origin.
watchList.evidence: ADR-008 line 46 answers T-02 with 'The runbook says so'; docs/ holds no RUNBOOK.md; PLAN.md names neither RUNBOOK nor Pages; .github/workflows holds only gate.yml; customer-list.js:5 says only 'Your data lives only in this browser'.
watchList.why_unproven: Nothing is published, so no user meets T-02 today; the missing file belongs to the devops role's future work, not to a built slice.
watchList.how_to_settle: Before the first publish, the devops role adds docs/RUNBOOK.md with the localhost-or-own-origin rule, and the human says whether the published app itself shows the demo-only note.

watchList.what_breaks: Two GitHub actions used in CI are named in no decision with an SPDX identifier, while ADR-001 says the project has no development dependencies.
watchList.evidence: gate.yml:15, :20 use actions/checkout@v7 and :27 actions/setup-node@v7; no docs/ file names them. LL-01 covers what the app ships and depends on; the actions run only in CI and are not redistributed.
watchList.why_unproven: Whether CI actions count as components under LL-01 is a scope decision, not a fact a test settles.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human says whether CI actions fall under LL-01; if yes, a decision names both with their SPDX id read from each repository (MIT).

equivalent.why: compareById is only reached as a tie-break between two different customers, whose ids are unique (shape.js:40 refuses duplicates, deps.newId is a UUID), so a.id === b.id never occurs and the equality branch never runs; sort uses only the sign.
-1 became -2: Array.prototype.sort reads only the sign of the comparator, so every order is unchanged.
Same reason as the < mutant: with unique ids the operands are never equal, so > and >= answer the same for every pair the sort passes.
-1 became -2: Array.prototype.sort reads only the sign of the comparator, so every order is unchanged.
The 0 branch is reached only when a.id === b.id, which unique ids rule out for any two distinct customers, so the value is never returned.

sumIsExact only tests Number.isSafeInteger(sum); subtracting every line total from 0 gives exactly the negation of the sum (IEEE 754 negation is exact and addition is sign-symmetric), and isSafeInteger is symmetric in sign, so the answer is identical for every input.
The line runs only inside if (a.date !== b.date), so the two date strings are never equal and < and <= give the same answer.
